topic: DFA FY2027 budget request, allotment classes, and utilization
summary: The DFA presented an FY2027 request of about 35 billion, while its stated net level for the department and attached agencies was 35,170,000,000, 17% above the 2026 net. Maintenance and other operating expenses accounted for 54% of the request, personnel services for 39%, and capital outlay for 7%; major items included next-generation passport funding, the International Commitments Fund, ATN and legal assistance, ICT, and the building fund. The agency reported an 80% 2025 BUR and close to 53% utilization in the first half of the current year, attributing lower performance to delayed retrofitting, transferred ATN functions, deferred building projects, and changing passport demand. Members requested detailed spending and program documents, particularly for the Security Council campaign, ATN Fund, ICT, and ePassport allocations. Rodriguez supported placing 250,000,000 for cybersecurity and restoring 300,000,000 to the building fund, while the Foreign Service Institute sought MXN 6,500,000 for HMO coverage. The committee left the additional funding requests for written submission and subsequent consideration, with a deadline set for the following Wednesday.
question: The committee sought to establish the DFA and attached agencies’ FY2027 funding requirement, the distribution of that request across allotment classes, the reasons for the increase, and the department’s utilization performance. Members also examined specific funding needs for passports, ICT and cybersecurity, buildings, consular operations, HMO, and permanent positions, and identified documents or augmentations to be submitted for further consideration.
agency_position: The DFA presented the FY2027 request as necessary to sustain overseas and consular services, implement the next-generation passport, strengthen ICT and cybersecurity, maintain overseas properties, and support foreign-policy operations. It reported strong physical performance but acknowledged utilization constraints and committed to submit requested budget, expenditure, and program documents.
outcome: The DFA’s proposed budget was presented and supported, but several augmentations and requests remained subject to written endorsement and later committee or plenary consideration. The agency committed to submit the requested ICT, ePassport, ATN, campaign-expenditure, and wish-list documents.

topic: Assistance to Nationals and Legal Assistance Funds for overseas Filipinos
summary: The committee asked the DFA to clarify ATN and LAF coverage, appropriations, utilization, eligibility rules, and approval authority after the DMW assumed responsibility for more OFWs. The DFA said 1,000,000,000 was appropriated annually for the ATN Fund from 2022 to 2025 and reported 2,884 ATN beneficiaries from January to July 2026, including 387 repatriation beneficiaries. It also cited welfare assistance of dollars 559,000,000, medical assistance of 20,000,000, and shipment of remains of 40,000,000, although some wording and currency attribution were unclear. The DFA said it generally did not deny qualified requests and that its office handled recommendations below 20%, while the Secretary approved amounts above that threshold. Members requested the ATN guidelines and detailed ATN and LAF utilization records, including balances, expenditures, approvals, rejections, nonqualifications, and beneficiaries. The DFA also described ongoing coordination on distressed seafarers and safe passage through embassies, MWOs, DMW, the IMO, and bilateral channels.
question: The committee sought to establish how the Assistance to Nationals (ATN) Fund and Legal Assistance Fund (LAF) were allocated, utilized, and administered, including which overseas Filipinos remained covered after the creation of the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW). It also sought beneficiary, expenditure, approval, rejection, eligibility, and utilization data, as well as the DFA's continuing assistance to distressed OFWs and seafarers.
agency_position: The DFA said ATN and LAF assistance remained available to distressed overseas Filipinos within the DFA's mandate, particularly in countries without MWOs and for categories such as tourists, students, pilgrims, permanent residents, and dual citizens. It said qualified requests were generally approved rather than denied, while the DMW increasingly handled OFWs as more MWOs opened.
outcome: The DFA explained the division of responsibility between the DFA and DMW and supplied partial ATN utilization and beneficiary figures. The committee requested additional ATN and LAF records and guidelines; the requested documentation was not submitted during the hearing.

topic: Consular-service expansion, satellite offices, and passport access
summary: Rep. Niko Raul Daza supported the DFA budget and cited the funded forty third consular office in Katarman, Northern Samar as an example of service expansion. The DFA reported 42 consular offices, more than 1.5 million passports processed, and 35 passport on wheels activities as of 08/31/2026. Rep. Eulogio Rodriguez asked the DFA to account for distance, isolation, travel costs, and accessibility in underserved provinces and specifically raised a possible satellite office in Catanhuanes. The DFA said it was assessing existing and proposed offices under operational, fiscal, geographic, DBM, and Executive Order 45 criteria, while studying a satellite model and offering passport on wheels in the interim. Bukidnon and Virac-Catanhuanes requests, consular vehicles, and facility funding remained under review. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez supported an additional building-fund request of about 300 million and other DFA requests, subject to written submissions and further budget consideration.
question: The committee sought to establish how the DFA was expanding access to consular services, particularly for provinces without a consular office, and whether new, satellite, or mobile facilities could address geographic isolation and travel costs. It also examined the funding and administrative requirements for proposed offices, vehicles, buildings, and related consular infrastructure.
agency_position: The DFA said it was conducting a nationwide assessment of existing and proposed consular facilities, balancing demand and accessibility against proximity, operational viability, fiscal sustainability, DBM guidance, and Executive Order 45. It had no established satellite-office model but was studying a smaller Catanhuanes facility, while offering passport on wheels as an interim option; requests for Bukidnon, Virac-Catanhuanes, vehicles, and additional building funds remained subject to review and coordination with DBM.
outcome: The DFA answered the accessibility and satellite-office questions and committed to provide a written status update and coordinate with DBM, while offering passport on wheels as an interim service. The proposed permanent facilities, vehicle requests, and funding augmentations were supported in principle but remained subject to DBM review and subsequent written budget action.

topic: ePassport budget of 5,500,000,000 and procurement breakdown
summary: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez presented passport funding as a major component of the DFA's proposed budget, including 2,800,000,000 for initial next-generation-passport funding and PHP 5,800,000,000 for passports overall. Representative Antonio Tinio then questioned the separate proposed ICT allocation of 956,610,000 and asked what the agency was actually purchasing. The ICT official described a shift toward large-scale capital assets, cited 511,000,000 in ICT projects, and identified the ePassport and passport appointment system among the covered systems. topic: West Philippine Sea diplomatic protests and China provisional arrangement
summary: Rep. Perci Cendaña asked the DFA to explain the written Philippines-China provisional arrangement for RORE missions, its negotiating authority, and whether it limited Philippine activities in the exclusive economic zone. Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro said it was an exchange of notes limited to Ayungin Shoal, without prejudice to Philippine positions under UNCLOS and the 2016 arbitral award, and focused on information exchange for daily necessities. She committed to making the arrangement's details available, and reported 16 RORE missions without incident over two years. Rep. Brian Poe asked about diplomatic protests, and DFA officials reported 39 protests in 2026 and 296 from 2022 to 2026, while noting that diplomacy could take time to produce results. In the second round, Rep. Antonio Tinio challenged Chinese Embassy statements concerning construction materials and the arbitral award; the DFA denied that construction materials were covered by the arrangement and said it raised concerns through diplomatic channels. The complete text and the DFA's response to each public embassy statement were not fully resolved in the hearing.

topic: UN Security Council campaign expenditures and outcome
summary: Representative Dada Kiram Ismula asked why the Philippines lost its bid for a nonpermanent UN Security Council seat and how much had been appropriated and spent on the campaign. topic: Critical Minerals Agreement review and US-Philippines economic relations
summary: Rep. Renee Co asked the DFA to submit the Critical Minerals Agreement or MOU with the United States and clarify whether the DFA had reviewed it. The DFA said the DENR led the agreement, with DTI and BOI involved, and that the DFA did not possess the document. DFA officials said the DENR and DTI had assessed the economic aspects, so the Office of International Economic Relations did not conduct a separate economic review, although the DFA concurred with the agreement. The agency said the arrangement could support value-added processing of copper and nickel, technological know-how, investment protection, and participation in chip, artificial-intelligence, and electric-vehicle applications. Rep. Co emphasized that the agreement had implications beyond one bilateral relationship and that the DFA should consider consistency with related agreements. The secretary committed to requesting the MOU from the concerned agency, but the scope of the DFA's review role remained partly unresolved.
question: The committee sought to establish whether the DFA had reviewed the Critical Minerals Agreement or MOU between the Philippines and the United States, what role it played in clearing or assessing the agreement, and whether it could provide the committee with a copy. outcome: The DFA did not provide the MOU during the hearing and said it would have to request the document from the concerned agency. topic: Repatriation of remains and overseas crisis assistance
summary: Rep. Brian Poe asked how the DFA was assisting Filipinos affected by the Nepal crisis and sought an update on Sam De La Cruz’s remains. The DFA said it was working through the New Delhi embassy and an honorary consul in Kathmandu, with one Filipino missing amid reports of about 4,000 missing persons. On De La Cruz’s case, the DFA explained that his remains had been buried in Bosaso after his death in July 2018, and that pandemic, legal, logistical, and diplomatic obstacles had stalled exhumation. The DFA committed to renewing instructions to its Nairobi embassy to pursue the case with Somali authorities. Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula then asked about ATN Fund use, and the DFA reported an annual appropriation of about 1 billion from 2022 to 2025, along with 2026 assistance figures including 387 repatriation beneficiaries and 2,884 total beneficiaries reported for the first six months. The member requested the ATN Fund guidelines, leaving the matter with a document submission and continued agency follow-up.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked whether the DFA had a complete list of Filipinos affected in Nepal and what assistance it was providing to Filipinos there.

thread.speaker: DFA Secretary
thread.said: She said the DFA had no foreign service establishment in Nepal and relied on the embassy in New Delhi, which had jurisdiction over Nepal, together with an honorary consul in Kathmandu. One Filipino was reported missing, and the DFA was working with international organizations and local authorities while seeking family DNA for matching with recovered bodies.

thread.speaker: DFA Secretary
thread.said: She said reports indicated about 4,000 missing persons in the Nepal crisis and that the search and identification process was continuing.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He raised the case of Sam De La Cruz, a 25-year-old migrant worker who died in 2018 while working on a fishing vessel and whose remains were reportedly buried in Somalia. He asked for an update on efforts to return the remains to the Philippines.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: The officer confirmed that Sam De La Cruz, a former seafarer registered with GMM Global Maritime in Manila, died in July 2018 from cardiopulmonary arrest. The DFA said the case was complicated by the COVID-19 pandemic, Somalia’s practice of immediate burial under Islamic Sharia, the absence of a Philippine mission in Somalia, and other logistical concerns.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: The Philippine embassy in Nairobi, which had responsibility for Somalia, had sent diplomatic notes but had not received an official reply from the Somali government. GMM had located the burial site in Bosaso and pursued permits and funding for exhumation, but negotiations with local officials stalled.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: He said Bosaso was about 1,000 kilometers from Mogadishu.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: He said that in 2025 the DFA had instructed the embassy in Nairobi to engage the Somali Embassy in Nairobi and convey the request to Mogadishu. Because no official reply had been received, the DFA would send instructions again to revive the matter.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He acknowledged the DFA’s tracking of the case and the difficulty caused by the lack of diplomatic ties and Somali nonresponse. He said the DFA should continue “knocking at their door” and assured migrant workers that the department would keep trying to bring home the remains.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: He asked about the ATN Fund and the total appropriations for assisting Filipinos in distress abroad from June 2022 to June 2026.

thread.speaker: DFA fiscal management official
thread.said: The official said that from 2022 to 2025, 1,000,000,000 was appropriated annually for the Assistance to Nationals Fund.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: He clarified that he wanted the 2026 figures for total ATN requests approved, denied, pending, and returned.

thread.speaker: DFA migrant affairs official
thread.said: For 2026, the official reported 387 beneficiaries for repatriation from January to July. The official also cited dollars 559,000,000 for welfare assistance, 20,000,000 for medical assistance, and 40,000,000 for shipment of remains, totaling 2,884 beneficiaries for the first six months of the year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: He asked for the specific guidelines and criteria used to approve or deny ATN requests, including the final approving authority.

thread.speaker: DFA migrant affairs official
thread.said: The official said a 2019 department order governed the ATN Fund and the Legal Assistance Fund. The office prepared recommendations for approvals involving certain amounts below 20%, while requests involving more than that were approved by the Secretary.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: He manifested a request that the DFA provide the committee a copy of the guidelines on the use of the ATN Fund.
